papers.title: Shank3 mutation disrupts the molecular signature of sleepiness across development
papers.summary: This study used RNA-sequencing on Shank3ΔC mutant mice to investigate the molecular basis of sleepiness across development. The mutation blocked age-typical recruitment of sleep deprivation response pathways at P24 and in adulthood, while elevating oxidative stress pathways, indicating impaired molecular response to sleepiness.

papers.title: Noradrenergic infraslow rhythm during sleep is the critical link between heart-rate dynamics and memory consolidation.
papers.summary: The study demonstrates that infraslow (~0.02 Hz) noradrenergic rhythms from the locus coeruleus drive heart rate fluctuations during NREM sleep, linking them to spindle activity and memory consolidation in both mice and humans. This identifies infraslow heart rate variability as a non-invasive marker of brainstem function and memory-promoting sleep.

papers.title: Theta oscillations tag episodic memories for sleep-dependent consolidation.
papers.summary: Using multivariate EEG classification in humans, the study decoded brain states for episodic memories tagged at learning for consolidation across sleep or wakefulness, linking tagging across sleep to 3-8 Hz theta rhythms during learning. Theta magnitude predicted slow oscillation-spindle coupling during post-learning sleep, which in turn was associated with enhanced memory performance, providing evidence for a neural tagging mechanism.

papers.title: Around the Clock: Wearing a Flex-Printed trEEGrid Electrode Patch and Miniaturized Amplifier for Nearly 24 Hours Across Daytime and Overnight EEG Sessions.
papers.summary: This study validated a novel flex-printed trEEGrid electrode patch and miniaturized amplifier for long-term (up to 24 h) EEG recordings on 10 participants, including daytime tasks and overnight sleep. The system showed comparable signal quality to ring electrodes for auditory N1 amplitudes and captured P3, resting state, and workload-related spectral effects on both days, supporting its utility for extended monitoring.

papers.title: Genuinely Blind Identification of Sleep Spindles through Trispectral Modulation Analysis
papers.summary: The paper introduces a blind, data-driven method using fourth-order spectrum (trispectrum) analysis to identify sleep spindles in EEG, achieving high agreement with expert annotation (median AUROC ~0.9) and detecting more spindle events than conventional methods. The method reveals that low-amplitude spindle-like bursting persists throughout NREM sleep and is suppressed in REM.

papers.title: [Research on electrooculography artifact removal from electroencephalography signals based on frequency slice wavelet transform].
papers.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
papers.summary: This paper proposes an improved frequency slice wavelet transform (FSWT) method for removing electrooculography (EOG) artifacts from single-channel EEG signals. The method achieved a mean signal-to-noise ratio improvement of 2.81 dB on all contaminated samples and 5.69 dB on strongly contaminated samples, while retaining theta-band energy at a rate of 0.889.

papers.title: The interplay between chronobiology, neuroinflammation, and the glymphatic system in neurodegenerative diseases.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence on the bidirectional crosstalk between circadian clocks, glial-mediated neuroinflammation, and glymphatic clearance, proposing that disruption of circadian timing contributes to neurodegeneration. It highlights melatonin as a potential multi-target chronotherapeutic agent to restore circadian rhythms and enhance glymphatic function.

papers.title: From plate to pillow: the role of food-derived bioactive compounds in sleep modulation and the potential of glia-neuron crosstalk.
papers.summary: This review evaluates five major categories of food-derived bioactive compounds (amino acids, polyphenols, fatty acids, bioactive peptides, and melatonin/indole derivatives) for sleep modulation. It proposes a periphery-to-center axis involving gut microbiota, blood-brain barrier, and glia-neuron crosstalk, highlighting glial cells as active regulators of sleep homeostasis.

papers.title: Non-linear and spectral EEG dynamics as stage-specific biomarkers of neuropsychological recovery post-stroke.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of 44 stroke patients and 25 controls found stage-specific changes in EEG fractal dimension and power spectral density during recovery, with right-hemisphere fractal dimension increases correlating with motor improvement. The results suggest that EEG biomarkers can inform stage-specific neurorehabilitation strategies.

papers.title: Shared Spectral Parameters Between EEG and Basal Ganglia LFP Distinguish Sleep-Specific Oscillations in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.summary: This study recorded simultaneous polysomnography and subthalamic nucleus local field potentials in 19 Parkinson's disease patients, finding that aperiodic spectral parameters (exponent and offset) differ between EEG and LFP across sleep stages and that STN-LFP aperiodic features alone classified sleep stages above chance. These findings suggest potential biomarkers for closed-loop neuromodulation targeting sleep dysfunction.

papers.title: Early Frontal qEEG Markers Predict Delayed Cognitive Recovery After Mild-to-Moderate Ischemic Stroke: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 96 stroke patients found that early frontal qEEG measures (lower PAF, reduced DTABR, elevated DFV) predicted delayed cognitive recovery at 3-6 months with good accuracy (AUC = 0.831). These markers could aid personalized rehabilitation planning.

papers.title: A preliminary investigation of the relationship between rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and fear inhibition processes in the context of circadian misalignment.
papers.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
papers.summary: In a randomized trial with 42 healthy adults, experimentally induced circadian misalignment predicted reduced REM sleep, and reductions in REM minutes predicted poorer extinction recall, suggesting circadian misalignment may impair fear inhibition via REM sleep loss.

papers.title: Non-Pharmacological Strategies in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Clinical Integration.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes mechanistic and clinical evidence on non-pharmacological strategies for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, covering dietary patterns, chrononutrition, microbiome modulation, and nutraceuticals, and highlights their synergistic effects with pharmacotherapy.

papers.title: LD-CNN19: A Deep Learning Model Integrating Logical Reasoning and Knowledge Expansion for Small-Sample Sleep Staging Tasks.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: The study proposes LD-CNN19, a neuro-symbolic deep learning framework for sleep staging that integrates logical reasoning and adaptive knowledge expansion, improving macro F1-scores by up to 4.22% and enhancing decision stability in small-sample settings.

papers.title: Phasic activities in the human body during REM sleep Part 1: Rapid eye movements and phasic muscle activity.
papers.summary: This review catalogs phasic activities during REM sleep, including rapid eye movements and muscle twitches, and discusses their putative functions. It highlights that some phasic activities occur more frequently in REM than NREM sleep, calling into question the distinct sub-phasing of REM sleep.

papers.title: Acupressure Potentially Promoting the Learning and Memory Capabilities of Hypoxic Ischemic Cerebral Palsy Rats.
papers.summary: In a rat model of hypoxic-ischemic cerebral palsy, acupressure treatment for 4 weeks improved learning and memory, enhanced hippocampal neuroplasticity (increased spine density, dendritic branching, and synaptic parameters), and partly restored EEG slow-wave activity and AMPAR/NMDAR protein expression. These results suggest acupressure promotes functional recovery in HIE.

papers.title: SleepStageNet: A Lightweight and Explainable Deep Learning Architecture for Multi-Channel Sleep Staging.
papers.summary: This study presents SleepStageNet, a compact deep learning model for automatic sleep staging from five PSG channels, evaluated on an Indian stroke cohort (95 subjects) achieving 73.91% accuracy and κ=0.634. Ablation studies showed C4-only input significantly reduced performance, while a 10-model ensemble generalized to ISRUC-SLEEP with κ=0.614 without fine-tuning.

papers.title: Evaluating Validation Strategies in Motor Imagery EEG: A Full-Cohort GAF-PLV Analysis and Matched Sensitivity Study.
papers.summary: This study evaluated validation strategies for motor imagery EEG classification, showing that random cross-validation overestimates performance compared to leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. On a full cohort (N=105), GAF-PLV achieved 58.07% accuracy, and model rankings varied by validation strategy, highlighting the need for subject-independent evaluation.

papers.title: Intraoperative EEG power spectrum alterations in patients with malignant brain tumors.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study, patients with malignant brain tumors undergoing craniotomy showed significantly lower absolute and relative beta band-power in intraoperative EEG compared to benign tumor and non-neurological control patients, while burst suppression incidence did not differ. This suggests distinct EEG alterations in malignant tumor patients.

papers.title: [Multi-view signal integration via manifold learning for sleep stage classification].
papers.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
papers.summary: The paper proposes a multi-view spatio-temporal convolutional integration network based on manifold learning for sleep stage classification, integrating EEG and other physiological signals. It outperforms existing mainstream methods on public datasets in accuracy, F1-score, and Kappa coefficient.

papers.title: The Relationship Between Chronotype and Depression Among Adolescents: The Mediating Role of Bedtime Procrastination and the Moderating Role of Parental Psychological Control.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 4324 adolescents found that chronotype is negatively associated with depression, with bedtime procrastination mediating 55.75% of the effect and parental psychological control moderating the relationships. The findings suggest multilevel interventions targeting sleep hygiene and family dynamics may reduce depressive risk.

papers.title: TARGETED MEMORY REACTIVATION DURING NON-RAPID EYE MOVEMENT SLEEP STRENGTHENS CONSOLIDATED DECLARATIVE MEMORIES
papers.summary: This study tested whether targeted memory reactivation (TMR) during NREM sleep can strengthen declarative memories learned 24 hours earlier. Participants receiving incomplete auditory reminders showed significantly less forgetting, despite comparable sleep architecture, and TMR was associated with increased slow oscillation and spindle activity, suggesting TMR benefits memories after consolidation.

papers.title: Acetazolamide Mitigates Opioid-Associated Sleep-Disordered Breathing.
papers.summary: In a crossover trial, acetazolamide (ACZ) significantly reduced apnea-hypopnea index (from 32.2 to 25.2 events/hour) and central apnea-hypopnea index (from 5.0 to 0.9 events/hour) in patients with opioid-associated sleep-disordered breathing. The reduction was driven by a decrease in plant gain due to ACZ-induced metabolic acidosis, while controller gain and cerebrovascular responsiveness were unchanged.

papers.title: Correlation study of polysomnographic parameters, serological markers, and gut microbiota in patients with short-sleep insomnia: a real-world study.
papers.summary: This real-world study compared polysomnographic parameters, serum markers, and gut microbiota between patients with short-sleep insomnia and controls. Insomnia patients showed altered sleep architecture, elevated serum 5-HT, BDNF, and orexin A, and distinct gut microbiota composition, with correlations among these factors suggesting gut-brain axis involvement.

papers.title: qEEG and Functional Connectivity as a Translational Bridge Between Humans and Dogs in Epilepsy and Associated Disorders: From Spontaneous Model to Automatic Classification-An Integrative Review.
papers.summary: This integrative review of 75 studies examines quantitative EEG (qEEG) and functional connectivity in humans and dogs with epilepsy and related disorders, highlighting the dog as a natural translational model. It finds cross-species similarities in EEG alterations and supports qEEG as a promising biomarker, though standardized validation is needed.

papers.title: Electrophysiological signatures of visual cortical dysfunction in Parkinson's disease: An integrative EEG-based review.
papers.summary: This integrative review synthesized human EEG-based studies on visual cortical dysfunction in Parkinson's disease, finding multilevel visual pathway dysfunction rather than a single cortex-specific biomarker. Prolonged P100 latency is the most reproducible finding, but ophthalmic and physiological confounders must be controlled.

papers.title: Neural processing of natural speech by adults with and without dyslexia: Evidence for atypical temporal sampling of speech information in the delta and theta EEG bands.
papers.journal: Cortex; a journal devoted to the study of the nervous system and behavior
papers.summary: This EEG study assessed neural tracking of natural speech in adults with and without dyslexia. Dyslexic adults showed less accurate delta- and theta-band decoding and reduced theta coherence, supporting atypical temporal sampling in dyslexia.

papers.title: Effect of electroencephalography-guided general anesthesia on postoperative delirium : A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of 18 randomized controlled trials evaluated the effect of EEG-guided anesthesia on postoperative delirium. EEG-guided anesthesia significantly reduced delirium incidence and EEG suppression duration, but had no significant effect on postoperative cognitive dysfunction.

papers.title: Brain activity alterations following lumbar discectomy in people with chronic low back pain.
papers.journal: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study used quantitative EEG to compare cortical activity in patients with chronic low back pain after lumbar discectomy versus healthy controls. Patients showed altered power in delta, theta, and alpha bands during pain-related visual stimulation, with source localization indicating changes in pain-processing regions.

papers.title: Umbilical Cord Mesenchymal Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes Alleviate Age-Related Insomnia in Rats by Suppressing Neuronal Ferroptosis in the Hippocampal Dentate Gyrus.
papers.summary: This study investigated whether umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (UCMSC-Exos) alleviate age-related insomnia in a rat model. UCMSC-Exos treatment reversed behavioral deficits, prolonged sleep, and reduced hippocampal neuronal ferroptosis, suggesting therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Psychobiological Correlates of Instructed Deceptive Responding: An Exploratory EEG Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory EEG study with 86 adults found that instructed deceptive responding was associated with increased right-frontal theta power, and trait anxiety positively correlated with self-reported deceptive behavior. Findings suggest involvement of executive control and conflict monitoring mechanisms.

papers.title: Objective Sleep Architecture Alterations and Sleep-Dependent Brain Clearance Dysfunction Across the Early Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Systematic Review.
papers.summary: This systematic review (4 studies) assessed the relationship between objectively measured sleep and glymphatic function across the Alzheimer's disease continuum. Better preserved slow-wave sleep and sleep oscillatory coupling were generally associated with more favorable brain clearance biomarkers, while disrupted sleep architecture was linked to impaired glymphatic clearance.

papers.title: Prunella vulgaris Compound Improves Sleep Architecture and Attenuates Hippocampal Injury in Insomnia Mice.
papers.summary: This study evaluated a Prunella vulgaris compound (PVC) in PCPA-induced insomnia mice. PVC shortened sleep latency, increased NREM and REM sleep, improved sleep continuity, attenuated hippocampal injury, modulated neurotransmitters (5-HT, GABA, glutamate, dopamine), and reduced NLRP3/caspase-1/GSDMD pyroptotic signaling.

papers.title: Ketone Ester Intake Did Not Improve Performance, Neither Cognitive Function or Sleep, During an 8-Day Simulated Cycling Race.
papers.journal: Medicine and science in sports and exercise
papers.summary: In a double-blind placebo-controlled trial with well-trained cyclists undergoing an 8-day simulated cycling race, ketone monoester supplementation did not improve performance, cognitive function, or sleep, despite increased fat oxidation and impaired mechanical efficiency.

papers.title: Effect of a Structured Preoperative Educational Video on Maternal Anxiety in Elective Cesarean Section: A Randomized Controlled Trial Using EEG Biomarkers.
papers.journal: Turkish journal of anaesthesiology and reanimation
papers.summary: In a randomized controlled trial of 90 primigravida women undergoing elective cesarean section, a structured preoperative educational video significantly reduced maternal anxiety as measured by APAIS scores and EEG-derived theta-beta ratio, and reduced intraoperative midazolam requirement.

papers.title: Association Between Glucocorticoid Exposure and Objective Sleep Architecture in Rheumatoid Arthritis: An Exploratory Pilot EEG Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory pilot study of 20 rheumatoid arthritis patients compared objective sleep architecture between glucocorticoid users and non-users using EEG and accelerometry. Glucocorticoid users had longer wake after sleep onset, shorter NREM stage N3 duration, and lower delta power despite comparable disease activity, suggesting an association with poorer sleep continuity and reduced deep sleep.

papers.title: Effect of Occupational Stress on Cognitive Functions Among Resident Doctors.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 281 postgraduate resident doctors found high occupational stress, particularly among clinical residents, which was associated with impaired attention, perception, and executive function, but not working memory.

papers.title: Corrigendum to "High-frequency rTMS mitigates acute sleep deprivation-induced anxiety-like behaviors and working memory impairments associated with hippocampal transcriptional modulation" [Neuroscience 602 (2026) 1-11].
papers.summary: This is a corrigendum to a previously published article; no new findings are reported.

papers.title: Spatially resolved transcriptional programs link fallopian tube precursor lesions to immune activation and stromal reorganization
papers.summary: This study generated a spatial transcriptomic atlas of fallopian tube carcinogenesis using Visium HD, mapping gene expression in normal epithelium, STIC, and invasive HGSC. They found that STIC lesions exhibit proliferation, replication stress, immune activation, and expression of tumor antigens PRAME and CLDN6, and that precursor lesions reside in immune-enriched, stromal-depleted microenvironments.

papers.title: Atrial Cardiomyopathy: Pathophysiology, Diagnostic Approaches, and Prognostic Implications-A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes the pathophysiology, diagnostic modalities, and prognostic implications of atrial cardiomyopathy, including structural, functional, and electrophysiological changes. It emphasizes the lack of standardized diagnostics and suggests that advanced imaging and biomarkers are promising for future risk stratification.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
